references.text: Jesus taught daily in the temple: "And he was teaching every day in the temple" ([ref:Luk 19:47|Luke 19:47]). This shows the same pattern of daily teaching in the temple mentioned in 21:37.

Jesus went to the Mount of Olives at night, as was his custom: "And he went out and made a habit of going to the Mount of Olives" ([ref:Luk 22:39|Luke 22:39]). This confirms the habit of spending nights on the Mount of Olives.
John describes the same pattern: Jesus went to the Mount of Olives at night and returned to the temple in the morning to teach ([ref:Joh 8:1-2|John 8:1-2]).
Matthew tells that Jesus left the city in the evening and stayed overnight in Bethany, which was located on the slope of the Mount of Olives ([ref:Matt 21:17|Matthew 21:17]).
Mark describes the same pattern where Jesus went out to Bethany in the evening and returned to Jerusalem the next morning ([ref:Mark 11:11-12|Mark 11:11-12]).

The next verse tells that the people came early in the morning to hear him in the temple ([ref:Luk 21:38|Luke 21:38]), which completes the picture of Jesus' daily rhythm of teaching during the day and withdrawing at night.
Jesus reminds them of his daily teaching in the temple: "Every day I sat in the temple and taught" ([ref:Matt 26:55|Matthew 26:55]). This confirms the pattern described in Luke 21:37.

Jesus says at his arrest: "While I was with you daily in the temple, you did not lay hands on me" ([ref:Luk 22:53|Luke 22:53]). This refers back to the period described in 21:37 of daily teaching in the temple.
